title: Revisiting deterministic motor sequence learning: EEG correlates and methodological challenges
title_zh: 重访确定性运动序列学习：EEG 相关指标与方法学挑战
abstract: Motor sequence learning refers to the transformation of discrete movements into integrated and automatized action patterns, underlying skill acquisition. Electroencephalography (EEG), with its high temporal resolution, enables the investigation of the neural dynamics underlying this process. However, despite a growing number of studies, findings remain fragmented and a framework of EEG correlates of deterministic motor sequence learning is still lacking. In this review, we critically examined twenty-three studies to characterize the EEG correlates associated with deterministic motor sequence learning. We aimed to disentangle sequence-specific neural changes from general practice effects, independently of participants' awareness of embedded regularities. We discuss key methodological aspects, including experimental design, control conditions, and awareness assessment. Despite substantial methodological heterogeneity and weaknesses in experimental control, electrophysiological findings converge on the view that learning reflects a shift toward more efficient processing. Learning-related changes include modulation of midline frontal negativities linked to performance monitoring, reductions in midline theta activity indicative of decreased top-down control demands, alpha-band alterations that may support improved stimulus prediction and motor preparation and beta activity, showing mixed general and sequence effects, supports response-related motor and cognitive plan shifts. Evidence on connectivity is more limited but points to reduced functional coupling during learning, while resting-state theta power and motor beta connectivity appear to predict training-related gains. By synthesizing current evidence, this review provides a critical appraisal of the field and recommendations for future research. contributing to a more consistent and interpretable framework for studying the neurophysiological basis of motor sequence learning.
abstract_zh: 运动序列学习（motor sequence learning）是将离散动作转化为整合且自动化动作模式的过程，构成技能获得的基础。脑电图（EEG）凭借高时间分辨率使研究该过程的神经动力学成为可能。然而，尽管研究数量不断增加，结果仍然支离破碎，尚未形成确定性运动序列学习的EEG相关框架。本文回顾性地检验了23项研究，系统刻画与确定性运动序列学习相关的EEG指标。我们旨在剥离由参与者对隐含规则意识之外的序列特异性神经变化和一般练习效应。我们讨论了关键方法学问题，包括实验设计、对照条件和意识评估。尽管方法学异质性和实验控制不足较大，电生理发现收敛于学习反映更高效加工的观点。学习相关变化包括：中线额区负向波动（与绩效监测相关）的调节、反映自上而下控制需求下降的中线θ活动减弱、可能支持刺激预测与运动准备的α频段变化，以及表现混合的一般/序列效应的β活动，支持反应相关运动与认知计划转变。连接性证据更有限，但提示学习期间功能耦合下降；而静息态θ功率与运动β连接似乎可预测训练收益。通过综合现有证据，本综述对该领域进行了批判性评估并提出未来研究建议，有助于建立更一致、可解释的框架研究运动序列学习的神经生理基础。
